_comment_canonical: CANONICAL in-tree PDVD TrackFitting configuration (doc pdvd/25 sec 7b). Consumed via the TaggerCheckSTM / TaggerCheckNeutrino 'trackfitting_config_file' knob. The path IS resolved through WIRECELL_PATH (Persist::resolve, TaggerCheckSTM.cxx:976-990), so 'pgrapher/experiment/protodunevd/pdvd_track_fitting.json' works; an absolute path passes through unchanged. Keys starting with '_' are skipped by load_trackfitting_config. Values are WCT internal units (mm, us; cm^2/s = 1e-7). Read at RUNTIME: a byte-identical compiled jsonnet does NOT mean the fit is unchanged.
_comment: Forked by duplication from sbnd/sbnd_track_fitting.json; only the six detector keys differ (DL, DT, add_sigma_L, ind_sigma_u_T, ind_sigma_v_T, col_sigma_w_T) -- exactly the uBooNE->SBND porting surface. Smearing sigmas MUST match the PDVD SP software filters (cfg/pgrapher/experiment/protodunevd/sp-filters.jsonnet; only Gaus_wide is consumed by OmnibusSigProc, Gaus_tight is dead config): add_sigma_L = 1/(2*pi*Gaus_wide 0.12 MHz) * drift 1.48073 mm/us = 1.32629 us * 1.48073 = 1.9639 mm; ind_sigma = (1/sqrt(pi)/Wire_ind 5.0) * 7.65 mm U/V pitch * {0.3 U, 0.5 V} = 0.2590 / 0.4316 mm; col_sigma = (1/sqrt(pi)/Wire_col 10.0) * 5.10 mm W pitch * 0.2 = 0.0575 mm. The trailing 0.2/0.3/0.5 factors are empirical uBooNE tunings kept on purpose (revisit with PDVD fit residuals). If the PDVD SP filters are retuned this file must be re-derived. The drift speed in add_sigma_L must be the one the grouping is configured with (TrackFitting reads it per (apa,face) from the grouping, TrackFitting.cxx:6840): the PR job must pass the runner's drift_speed_bot/top_mmus TLAs (1.48073, run_clus_evt.sh). A job falling back to the 1.568 jsonnet default mis-scales this term by 6 %. Hazard: PDVD sets drift speed PER CRATE but this file is global -- if the two crates are ever calibrated apart, add_sigma_L cannot follow. Everything else is inherited from SBND/uBooNE unchanged (selection knobs, min_drift_time floor 50 us, div_sigma).
_comment_diffusion: DL/DT are PHYSICAL PDVD transport coefficients from the BNL LAr-properties parameterisation (lar.bnl.gov/properties; pdvd/stm/pdvd_transport.py) evaluated at the ADOPTED production drift field E = 0.45 kV/cm (450 V/cm, owner decision 2026-09-03, doc pdvd/29), T = 87.3 K (site default) -> DL = 4.1307 cm^2/s, DT = 7.9135 cm^2/s (4.1307e-7 / 7.9135e-7 internal). Supersedes the 2026-09-02 version (E = 0.439 kV/cm derived from the data-calibrated drift velocity v = 1.48073 mm/us at T = 87.68 K -> DL = 4.123, DT = 7.824): the field is now set directly rather than derived from velocity, and the drift speed itself (production 1.48073 mm/us, params.jsonnet default 1.568 mm/us) was NOT changed to match -- under the same parameterisation neither currently inverts to exactly 0.45 kV/cm; see doc pdvd/29 for the flagged inconsistency. Unlike SBND (doc 66 reverted to the sim pair 4.0/8.8 for MC consistency), PDVD runs on DATA in this campaign, so the physical values apply; the PDVD sim (simparams.jsonnet) still drifts with 4.0/8.8 -- on MC this file mis-models the waveforms and an MC arm must use the sim pair.
_comment_skip_revert_iso_xext_cut: doc pr/28 sec 17 round 10 (toolkit 6b219d14). C++ default -1 (off, unconditional revert). 200.0 = 20 cm (units::cm=10) -- SBND production default (inherited by PDVD unchanged) since 2026-08-06 (owner: 'overall better, please turn it on for these for SBND', gate work-pr28r10-flip vs -on48b single-event byte-identical; population gate work-pr28r10-on48b vs -off48b already on record, doc pr/28 sec 17.4 G4/G5). Abstains from skip_trajectory_point's charge-consistency revert when the point's cluster has blob-center drift-x extent below this cut -- i.e. isochronous clusters only; non-isochronous clusters (including doc pr/28 sec 13's evt 388) are unconditionally unaffected.
_comment_good_point_pitch_frac: doc pdvd/32 round 3, owner decision 2026-09-04: PDVD PRODUCTION. Per-plane floor on the trajectory END TRIM's good-point radius, as a fraction of that plane's wire pitch -- examine_end_ps_vec's is_good_point uses max(0.2 cm, frac*pitch[plane]). The ctpc is an exact (drift-step x pitch) lattice, so at PDVD's 0.765 cm U/V pitch the shipped 0.2 cm spans 0.52 of a pitch and an interior trajectory point passes the strict three-plane test only 17.5 % of the time, against 62.4 % at SBND's 0.300 cm; the trajectory was losing a median 22.1 cm across its two ends. C++ default 0 = off, so this key is what turns it on and ONLY for PDVD -- sbnd_track_fitting.json is untouched and every other detector keeps the legacy radius. 0.35 was chosen over the larger values because max() only moves a plane once frac*pitch exceeds 0.2 cm: at 0.35 the only plane that changes on any detector is PDVD U/V (0.268 cm), while PDVD W, PDHD, SBND and uBooNE all stay at 0.200 cm. Keeping W pinned is what holds the trajectory on real charge -- above frac 0.392 (= 0.2/0.510) W unpins and the loosened trim stops masking the endpoint-selection defect of doc 32 sec 2.2, growing a 45 cm excursion onto a branch. Do NOT raise this above 0.39 without fixing endpoint selection first.
